content: 1. The pharmacokinetics and placental transfer of antiretroviral drugs, including elvitegravir and dolutegravir, were studied during pregnancy to assess their safety and efficacy. 2. Dolutegravir was evaluated for its pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy in HIV-positive children aged 2 to less than 6 years, with findings presented at a major conference. 3. A study on African children with HIV weighing ≥25 kg demonstrated the pharmacokinetics and early safety of switching to 50 mg film-coated dolutegravir tablets as part of the ODYSSEY trial. 4. The safety and effectiveness of dolutegravir in children and adolescents with HIV in the UK and Ireland were analyzed, with results shared at an international workshop. 5. The pharmacokinetics, safety, and 48-week efficacy of oral raltegravir were studied in HIV-1-infected children aged 2 to 18 years, with findings published in a clinical journal. 6. Raltegravir for oral suspension was evaluated for its pharmacokinetics, safety, and efficacy over 48 weeks in HIV-1-infected children aged 4 weeks to 2 years. 7. A population pharmacokinetic analysis of raltegravir pediatric formulations was conducted in HIV-infected children aged 4 weeks to 18 years. 8. The pharmacokinetics and safety of raltegravir in HIV-1-exposed neonates were studied in a dose-finding study under the IMPAACT P1110 protocol. 9. Raltegravir-based therapy was explored for its potential to induce rapid viral decay in highly viremic HIV-infected neonates. 10. A Phase I/II study investigated the use of raltegravir-containing regimens in HIV/TB co-treated children, with results presented at a conference. 11. A systematic review and meta-analysis examined the clinical use of HIV integrase inhibitors, including dolutegravir, highlighting their efficacy and safety. 12. Dolutegravir pharmacokinetics were studied in pregnant and postpartum women living with HIV to understand its safety and dosing requirements. 13. The presence of dolutegravir in breast milk and its levels in maternal and infant plasma during breastfeeding were analyzed. 14. Neural-tube defects associated with dolutegravir treatment from conception were reported in a study published in a leading medical journal. 15. A comparative safety study in Botswana evaluated dolutegravir-based versus efavirenz-based antiretroviral treatment initiated during pregnancy. 16. The etiology, pathogenesis, and prevention of neural tube defects were reviewed in a congenital anomalies journal. 17. The safety and efficacy of dolutegravir-based ART in TB/HIV co-infected adults were assessed at week 24 in a clinical study. 18. A Phase 1 study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of dolutegravir administered with rifampin or rifabutin in healthy subjects. 19. Cytokine-mediated systemic adverse drug reactions were observed in a study of dolutegravir interactions with isoniazid and rifapentine. 20. A cost-savings analysis of a candidate universal antiretroviral regimen was conducted to evaluate its economic impact. 21. A cost-utility analysis compared dolutegravir to raltegravir in treatment-naive and treatment-experienced patients in Slovakia. 22. The cost-effectiveness of dolutegravir in HIV-1 treatment-naive and treatment-experienced patients in Canada was analyzed. 23. Updated recommendations on first-line and second-line antiretroviral regimens and post-exposure prophylaxis were provided, along with early infant HIV diagnosis guidelines. 24. A cost-utility analysis of dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine as a single-tablet regimen for naive HIV-infected patients was conducted. 25. The cost-effectiveness of dolutegravir plus abacavir/lamivudine versus efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine for first-line HIV-1 treatment in the United States was evaluated. 26. The cost-effectiveness of dolutegravir in HIV-1 treatment-experienced patients in France was analyzed. 27. The cost impact of replacing efavirenz with dolutegravir in first-line antiretroviral treatment for adults in South Africa was assessed. 28. A cost-utility analysis of the fixed-dose combination of dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine as initial treatment for HIV-positive patients in Spain was conducted. 29. A cost-effectiveness analysis compared dolutegravir plus backbone regimens to other antiretroviral therapies in treatment-naive and experienced HIV-positive patients. 30. The cost-effectiveness of dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine in treatment-naive HIV-1 patients in France was reviewed. 31. The cost-effectiveness and budgetary impact of a dolutegravir-based regimen as first-line treatment for HIV in India were analyzed. 32. The benefits and risks of antiretroviral therapy for perinatal HIV prevention were reviewed in a prominent medical journal. 33. Surveillance of HIV drug resistance in adults receiving ART was conducted to monitor acquired resistance patterns. 34. A study compared dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine to current ART in virally suppressed patients, demonstrating non-inferiority over 48 weeks. 35. Switching from a boosted protease inhibitor-based regimen to a dolutegravir regimen in virologically suppressed patients with high cardiovascular risk or age >50 years was shown to be non-inferior and reduced lipid levels. 36. A meta-analysis of dolutegravir in 13 randomized trials involving 7,340 patients assessed its efficacy and safety in relation to current HIV RNA suppression. 37. The global epidemiology of drug resistance following failure of WHO-recommended first-line regimens for adult HIV-1 infection was studied. 38. Routine viral load monitoring in HIV-infected infants and children in lowand middle-income countries was reviewed, highlighting challenges and opportunities. 39. The choice of antiretroviral drugs for continued treatment scale-up in resource-limited settings was discussed in a public health approach. 40. A pilot study evaluated dolutegravir plus lamivudine for initial treatment of HIV-1-infected participants with HIV-1 RNA <500,000 copies/mL. 41. HIV-1 DNA ultra-deep sequencing analysis was performed at the initiation of dual therapy with dolutegravir and lamivudine in a maintenance pilot study.
